nodes.statement: Recall that Claims~,~, proven in,, are analogous to these propositions, but set in C. We want to show why they imply that these propositions hold in Sigma. The proofs for both propositions are very similar, so we present them simultaneously. Let tildegamma: S^1 to Sigma be a closed orbit of (i_2)_* xi_k,w(t) in the class tau_i_2(alpha_k,w) (or tau_i_2(alpha_k^prime), in the case where k in K) such that z = tildegamma(0) is a non-degenerate fixed point of (i_2)_* Xi_k(w). By Claim~, if k is large enough then z in i_2(C), therefore y = i_2^-1(z) in C is uniquely defined. Denote by tildegamma_y : S^1 to C the xi_k,w(t)-orbit of y. By Claim~, there exist k_1,...,k_r, l_1,...,l_r in Z , u_1,...,u_r, v_1,...,v_r in \0,1\ such that \[ [tildegamma_y]_pi_0(LC) = eta_C,s_0(Pi_m=1^r a^k_mc^-u_mb^l_mc^v_m) . \] Since tau_i_2([tildegamma_y]_pi_0(LC)) = [tildegamma]_pi_0(LSigma) = tau_i_2(alpha_k,w) (or tau_i_2(alpha_k^prime)), one has [tildegamma_y]_pi_0(LC) = alpha_k,w (or [tildegamma_y]_pi_0(LC) = alpha_k^prime) by Claim~. Thus non-degenerate fixed points of (i_2)_* Xi_k(w) in Sigma whose orbits are in the class tau_i_2(alpha_k,w) correspond in a 1-1 manner to non-degenerate fixed points of Xi_k(w) in D whose orbits are in the class alpha_k,w (and there is a similar correspondence for the classes tau_i_2(alpha_k^prime),alpha_k^prime). Note that since Claim~ uses Lemma~, this is the point where the algebraic Lemma~ enters the proof. \\ Therefore it is enough to restrict the analysis to the dynamics on D, and further, to the dynamics on C, since z in i_2(C). In order for the concept of cyclically reduced elements of F_3 to be defined, consider F_3 = langle a,b,c rangle as the free product left langle left langle R right rangle * left langle S right rangle right rangle, for some two proper subsets R bigsqcup S = \a,b,c\. Therefore there exists a proper partition R bigsqcup S = \a,b,c\ such that len_R,S(x) geq 2 or len_R,S(y) geq 2.
